dedupe_keys.name: duke energy hot springs microgrid islanding during hurricane helene

description: This conference session page from T&D World Live 2025 describes how Duke Energy's Hot Springs microgrid in North Carolina was used after Hurricane Helene in 2024. The microgrid deployed its islanding capabilities to restore service to a remote mountain community, well beyond the scope it was designed for, and the talk by Trent Miller of Duke Energy covers off-grid load segmentation and protection schemes. The session ran on 23 September 2025. Coverage is one small community and one storm; the page is free to read, gives no capacities or outage counts and states no licence. Caveats: only the session abstract was read, so technical details, restoration times and any measured data are not available here, and slides may need conference registration. For simulation, it is a documented operating case for resilience and emergency response studies of microgrids that island and serve communities cut off by storm damage. Related catalogue record: case_study-borrego-springs-microgrid-100-percent-renewable-blackstart-sdge-nrel.
